newsitem.title: CANADA: Crystallex says Venezuela proposes deal.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex says Venezuela proposes deal.

text.p: Crystallex International Corp President Marc Oppenheimer said on Friday that senior Venezuelan officials had tried to promote a deal between the company and Placer Dome Inc to resolve the ownership controversy over the gold-rich Las Cristinas concession.

"There have been some overtures to that end. Certain representatives of the (Venezuelan) government, some ministers, have discussed this. It is one of multiple options," Oppenheimer told the annual meeting.
Venezuelan officials suggested a joint venture with Placer or possibly a takeover bid by Placer, Oppenheimer said.
He declined to confirm or deny whether Crystallex was in negotiations with Placer or any other company.
"We don't have anything in writing," Oppenheimer said.
Crystallex and Placer have been in a legal battle over the ownership of Las Cristinas, South America's largest gold mine.
Crystallex has said it owns the two Cristinas concessions after it bought local company Inversores Mael last year.
Placer and Venezuelan state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) also claim ownership of the concessions.
Oppenheimer said Crystallex was awaiting a fourth and hopefully final ruling by the Venezuelan Supreme Court on the dispute by the end of July.
He said he was optimistic the next ruling would resolve the ownership controversy once and for all.
"It will correct certain administrative deficiencies of the past. We don't think there will be any additional rulings required," Oppenheimer said.
